# Lesson 1 · Your Okta org

=== "Theory"

    An Okta **org** is one environment. It holds the users, groups, app integrations, and policies you work with. Your Integrator org has its own records and settings. A Workforce trial has its own records and settings too. If you open the trial and search for a user you created in your Integrator org, that user record will still be in the Integrator org. The org you open determines which data and settings you see.

    That makes the org name and hostname the first things to check before you investigate an issue or change a setting. Okta's standard Admin Console hostname includes `-admin`. The org hostname and its corresponding admin hostname can lead to different views of the same environment. The **Admin Console** is where you manage the org. The **End-User Dashboard** shows app tiles for the signed-in user.

    ## What Okta knows about a user

    A **user account** is the record Okta keeps for a user in that org. Part of that record is the **profile**. It holds values such as the login, email address, and department. Each field is called an **attribute**.

    The account also has a **status**. Status tells you where the account is in its lifecycle. A department value tells you something about the user. The account status tells you something about the account itself. When you open **Directory → People**, look for both. You will use them for different checks.

    ## How a profile value becomes group membership

    A **group** is a collection of users. It lets you manage a set of people together. When you open a group, its membership tells you which users currently belong to it.

    There are two useful ways to think about how a user gets there. An administrator can add the user directly. An administrator can also configure a **group rule** so Okta manages membership based on a condition.

    A group rule has a condition and a target group. For an attribute-based rule, Okta reads the value from the user's Okta profile. If the rule is active and the user meets its conditions, Okta can add the user to the target group. The profile supplies the value. The rule makes use of that value. The membership is the result you can inspect.

    If the membership you expected is missing, start with the profile value Okta actually has. Then open **Directory → Groups → Rules** and check the condition, whether the rule is active, and which group it targets. Finally, open the group itself to see the membership. Each screen answers a different question.

    ## How group membership leads to an app assignment

    An **app integration** is the configuration that represents a connection to an application in Okta. An **assignment** makes that integration available to a user. You can assign the integration directly to the user or assign it to a group so members receive it through the group.

    Follow those two relationships in order. First, establish that the user is in the group. Then open the app integration and establish that the group is assigned. Both relationships are needed for this path. A user can also have an assignment through a different group or a direct assignment, so check the source of the assignment before explaining why the user has it.

    You can inspect this from **Applications and Resources → Applications**. Open an app integration and select **Assignments**. That view helps you understand who receives the integration. Later, when we study provisioning, we will check separately whether the connected application has an account for the user.

    ## What happens when the user opens the app

    An app assignment answers one question: is this integration available to the user in Okta? When the user opens an app that Okta protects, a second question matters: has the user met the sign-in requirements for this app?

    **Authentication** is how the user proves their identity. After Okta accepts a sign-in, it can establish a **session** so the browser can continue as that user. The **global session policy** sets the requirements for establishing that Okta session.

    When the user opens an app, Okta also checks the **app sign-in policy** for that app. This policy specifies the proof needed to open the app. For example, the existing Okta session might already carry the proof the app requires. If the app requires additional proof, the user can see another prompt even though the dashboard is already open.

    This gives you a starting point when something looks wrong. Check the assignment when you need to explain how the user received the integration. Check the sign-in policy and the sign-in event when you need to explain an authentication prompt or denial. If Okta sign-in succeeds and the application still denies a particular action, the application's own permissions may need checking.

    ## Where to see each part

    **People** and **Groups** appear under the same **Directory** menu. Open **People** to inspect one account and its profile. Open **Groups** to inspect who belongs to a group and which rules can manage that membership.

    <img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="950" height="216" alt="Admin Console sidebar and People page with the user search field">

    | What you want to establish | Where to look |
    | --- | --- |
    | Which org you opened | Check the org name and browser hostname. |
    | Which status and profile values the user has | Open the user under **Directory → People**. |
    | Which users belong to a group | Open the group under **Directory → Groups**. |
    | What condition drives membership | Open **Directory → Groups → Rules**. |
    | How the app integration is assigned | Open the integration under **Applications and Resources → Applications**, then select **Assignments**. |
    | What the user sees | Open the **End-User Dashboard** as that user. |

    ## Check your understanding

    1. Why can two orgs show different results when you search for the same login?
    2. You can see the expected profile value. Which records would you check to establish whether that value led to an app assignment?
    3. Why can a user who already signed in to Okta receive an additional prompt when opening an assigned app?

    Try each answer in your own words before reopening the relevant section. In the next lesson, you will see how an account moves through activation and how to check its status.

=== "Hands-on Lab"

    ## Lab 1 · Find your way around Okta

    Sign in to your Integrator org with your administrator account. This walkthrough opens pages and reads what is already there.

    If you are reading without an org, follow the screenshot and page descriptions to see where each kind of information lives. You can return to the steps when you have access.

    ### 1. Open the Admin Console and End-User Dashboard

    <img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="448" height="156" alt="Admin Console toolbar with the Okta apps button and My end user dashboard menu">

    1. Open your Integrator org. If Okta takes you to the **End-User Dashboard**, select **Admin** near the top of the page. If sign-in takes you to the **Admin Console**, you are ready for the next step.
    2. In the Admin Console header, open **Okta apps** and select **My end user dashboard**. Use this menu if opening the dashboard directly sends you back to the console. [Okta Support explains this Integrator redirect](https://support.okta.com/help/s/article/okta-integrator-administrator-is-redirected-to-the-admin-console-when-accessing-the-end-user-dashboard).
    3. Compare what each page shows. The console has navigation such as **Directory** and **Applications and Resources**. The dashboard shows apps available to the signed-in account. The standard console hostname also includes `-admin`. Return to the Admin Console for the remaining steps.

    ### 2. Find a user and inspect the profile

    1. In the left sidebar, expand **Directory**, then select **People**.
        The **People** page has a search field above the user list.

        <img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="950" height="216" alt="Admin Console sidebar and People page with the user search field">

    2. Find your account by name or login in the People list. Read its **Status**.
    3. Select your name to open the user record, then choose **Profile**. Look for **First name** or **Login**. These fields describe the user. Status describes the account's lifecycle state.

    ### 3. Find group members and group rules

    **Directory → Groups → Everyone.** The group name and **Back to Groups** tell you that you have opened an individual group. Select **People** to see its members.

    <img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="950" height="275" alt="Directory sidebar and Everyone group with the People tab">

    **Directory → Groups.** Back on the page titled **Groups**, select **Rules** beside **All**.

    <img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="950" height="229" alt="Directory sidebar and Groups page showing All and Rules">

    1. In the sidebar, go to **Directory → Groups**. On the Groups page, open **Everyone** or another group already in your org.
    2. Select **People** on the group page to see its members. This tab shows the people in that group. **Directory → People** opens the org's user list.
    3. Go back to **Directory → Groups** and select **Rules** on the Groups list. This is where Okta lists group rules for the org. An empty list is fine. You will create a rule in Lab 3.

    ### 4. Find app assignments

    <img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="950" height="281" alt="Admin Console sidebar and Applications page with its search field">

    1. In the sidebar, expand **Applications and Resources**, then select **Applications**.
    2. Select the name of an existing app integration to open its settings. Select **Assignments** and look for **People** and **Groups**. These views show the users and groups assigned to that integration.
    3. If you cannot find an integration with an **Assignments** tab, stop at the Applications list. You will return to that tab when you configure an integration in Lab 4. [Manage app integration assignments](https://help.okta.com/oie/en-us/Content/Topics/apps/apps-manage-assignments.htm)

    [See Okta’s screenshot of the Assignments tab with People and Groups filters](https://support.okta.com/help/s/article/How-to-see-from-which-group-the-user-inherits-the-assignment-for-an-app).
